title: Five Crazy Government Experiments
summary: Josh and Chuck cover five crazy government experiments: the Raytheon/Percy Spencer microwave origin as a warm-up; Charles Guthrie's two-headed dog (1908); Soviet head transplants on dogs by Vladimir Demikhov, including the 1940s revived-dog film and the 1970 Robert J. White monkey head transplant; CIA's Acoustic Kitty cat surveillance program during the Cold War; the Nazi "Bell" zero point energy/anti-gravity claims promoted by Nick Cook; NASA and Soviet space sex research claims, including Valentina Tereshkova's pregnancy and the Two Suit; and Soviet/US psychic spy research leading to Project Stargate. The episode closes with listener mail about pica and a traveling vacuum salesman in Geneva near CERN, and a sign-off.
topics: Robert J. White monkey head transplant

segments.title: Opening banter and microwave origin
segments.summary: Hosts open the show, then Josh recounts how Percy Spencer discovered microwaves near a magnetron at Raytheon, as a lead-in to the idea of government experiments.

segments.title: Head transplants: two-headed dog and Soviet experiments
segments.summary: Charles Guthrie's 1908 two-headed dog, a 1940s revived-dog film, and Vladimir Demikhov's puppy head transplants in the Soviet Union, with some animals surviving up to 29 days.

segments.title: Robert J. White monkey head transplant
segments.summary: In 1970, Robert J. White transplanted one monkey's head onto another monkey's body; the monkey survived about a week before being put down.

segments.title: Acoustic Kitty
segments.summary: The CIA spent years and millions trying to turn a cat into a surveillance device; the cat was killed by a cab on its first mission, and the program was declassified in 2001 with redactions.

segments.title: Zero point energy and the Nazi Bell
segments.summary: Explanation of zero point energy from quantum mechanics, and the claim by Nick Cook that Nazi researchers built an anti-gravity device, the so-called Nazi Bell, passed to the US; follow-up claims by Tim Bentura and American Anti Gravity are mentioned.

segments.title: Sex in space and the Two Suit
segments.summary: Claims that NASA and Soviet programs researched sexual activity in zero gravity, including Pierre Kohler's book and Valentina Tereshkova's pregnancy, followed by a discussion of the Two Suit designed by Vana Bonta.

segments.title: Psychic spies and Project Stargate
segments.summary: Soviet and US paranormal research, a Rand-style comparison concluding the Soviets were more scientific, and Project Stargate's remote viewers.

segments.title: Listener mail: pica and a vacuum salesman
segments.summary: A listener shares childhood craving for match heads (pica), and another listener reports being a traveling vacuum salesman in Geneva near CERN.

segments.title: Sign-off
segments.summary: Hosts invite emails about the movie The Thing with Two Heads and visits to CERN, then close the episode.
